source_book: Sri Chaitanya — IPE STUDY MATERIAL for Jr. Students, Chemistry (2026-27 edition)
note: Question index for diffing and authoring. Sections: VSAQ 32 numbers / 35 questions (Q17 has four parts), SAQ 12 numbers / 14 questions (Q42, Q43 have two parts each), LAQ 7 numbers / 9 questions (Q50, Q51 have two parts each), PROBLEM 18 numbers / 22 questions (1.5 two parts, 1.18 four parts) — 80 entries. The scan is clean apart from a clipped left margin on scan page 2 (the leading digit of question 18 is cut) and a partly obscured label on problem 1.12. Stems restated in our own wording with the chemistry exact; no solution content from the source book appears in this file, by policy.

questions.stem: State the charge, the mass and the charge-to-mass ratio of an electron.
Calculate the number of electrons that together weigh one gram.
Calculate the mass and the charge of one mole of electrons.
Calculate the mass of one mole of protons.
Calculate the mass of one mole of neutrons.
How many neutrons and how many electrons are present in each of carbon-13 (Z = 6), oxygen-16 (Z = 8), magnesium-24 (Z = 12), iron-56 (Z = 26) and strontium-88 (Z = 38)?
questions.notes: The book prints the nuclide symbols ¹³₆C, ¹⁶₈O, ²⁴₁₂Mg, ⁵⁶₂₆Fe, ⁸⁸₃₈Sr and asks for the neutrons and electrons 'in the nuclei'; electrons are not in a nucleus, so read it as the neutral atom of each nuclide.

questions.stem: Explain the difference between emission spectra and absorption spectra.

The quantum numbers of four electrons are: (a) n = 4, l = 2, mₗ = 2, mₛ = +1/2; (b) n = 3, l = 2, mₗ = −1, mₛ = −1/2; (c) n = 4, l = 1, mₗ = 0, mₛ = +1/2; (d) n = 3, l = 1, mₗ = −1, mₛ = −1/2. Arrange them in order of increasing energy.
questions.notes: (a) to (d) label the four electrons, not sub-questions; one entry.
